rejected.title: Qualitative movement analysis
card: Prepare
before watching, decide which skill to analyse, learn what good technique looks like, and plan where to stand and what to record.
Observe
watch the movement and judge it by eye, without measuring it with numbers. Watch it several times and from different angles. Video can be used to replay it.
Evaluate
compare what was seen with the ideal technique. Find the main error and its likely cause.
Correct
give feedback or a drill that fixes the cause of the error. Then watch the movement again to check it has improved.
rejected.remember: Judge the movement by eye against a good model, find the cause of the error, then fix it and check again.

a.q: After filming a netball shot, a coach holds the clip up against a model of good technique to work out what went wrong. Which step is this?
a.why: Comparing what was seen with good technique to find the error and its cause is the evaluate step. Observe is tempting, but it is only the watching and filming. The judging comes after it.
a.clue: The coach has already watched. Now they are judging.

b.q: Coach Priya films Sam bowling from the front and side. Against good technique, she finds he rushes his run-up, so his arm drops. She says 'good effort' and ends the session. Which step was weak?
b.why: Priya found the error and its cause, so she evaluated well. She then gave no feedback or drill to fix it and did not watch again, so the correct step was weak. Evaluate is tempting, but working out the cause is exactly what she did well.
b.clue: What should happen after the cause of an error is found?

draft.title: Qualitative movement analysis
card: Qualitative movement analysis is a coach or teacher judging the quality of a movement by watching it, without measuring it with numbers. It is used to improve a skill.
Prepare
decide what skill to look at, learn what a good performance looks like, and plan where to stand and what to record.
Observe
watch the movement, often several times and from different angles. Video can be used to replay it.
Evaluate and correct
compare what was seen with the ideal technique to find the error and its likely cause. Then give feedback or a drill to fix it, and watch again.
draft.remember: Prepare, observe, evaluate, correct: judge the movement against a good model, then fix the cause of the error.

a.q: Which step of qualitative movement analysis is a coach doing when they compare a netball shot with the ideal technique to find the error?
a.why: Comparing what was seen with the ideal technique to find the error is the evaluate step. Observe is tempting, but it is only the watching. The judging comes after it.
a.clue: The coach has already watched. Now they are judging.

b.q: Coach Priya watches Sam's cricket bowling from the side only, and then gives advice about his front arm, which she could not see well. Which part of the analysis was weak?
opts: Preparing a plan to correct the error
Correcting the error with a drill
Measuring his speed with a radar gun
b.why: The card says to watch from different angles. Watching from the side only meant she could not see his front arm well, so her advice rested on poor observation. Radar measurement is numbers, which is not qualitative analysis.
b.clue: What did she see, and from where?

problems.detail: The right option, 'Observing from one angle only', echoes the stem's 'from the side only'. It is also the only option worded as a flaw, so a student can match it without knowing the steps.

The card puts evaluate and correct together in one bullet, but the remember line splits them into four separate steps. Question a then depends on telling evaluate from correct, so the card should present them as separate steps too.
